title: A spare Renault Twingo in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez: why it still feels right
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: In the gulf, short trips, quick parking and collecting visiting relatives still favour a light, simple and immediately understandable car such as our Twingo Helios.
content:
The cars that matter are not always the ones that travel far. In the Gulf of Saint-Tropez, a small available car that is easy to park and easy to lend can often give more service than a more ambitious machine.

A short, simple and clear car

The first Twingo keeps dimensions that suit short trips perfectly. It is easy to place, quick to understand and comfortable to take in hand. For a spare car, that obviousness is worth a great deal.

This is not an abstract quality. It is the basis of regular use without fatigue or complication.

Why it works well in the gulf

Short runs, useful errands, collecting guests and sometimes tight parking all fit the Twingo very well. It holds its place without trying to look more important than it is.

The Helios sunroof even adds a little pleasure that suits the local climate and rhythm well.

A classic for use, not for display

We do not keep this car in order to show it. We keep it because it serves. That difference changes everything in the way one maintains and reads it.

The Twingo then remains faithful to its best programme: making life simpler with modest means and real accuracy.
